verses.eng: 95:2 Sing ye to the Lord and bless his name: * shew forth his salvation from day to day.

verses.lat: 95:3 Annuntiáte inter gentes glóriam ejus, * in ómnibus pópulis mirabília ejus.
verses.eng: 95:3 Declare his glory among the Gentiles: * his wonders among all people.

verses.lat: 95:4 Quóniam magnus Dóminus, et laudábilis nimis: * terríbilis est super omnes deos.
verses.eng: 95:4 For the Lord is great, and exceedingly to be praised: * he is to be feared above all gods.

verses.lat: 95:5 Quóniam omnes dii géntium dæmónia: * Dóminus autem cælos fecit.
verses.eng: 95:5 For all the gods of the Gentiles are devils: * but the Lord made the heavens.

verses.lat: 95:6 Conféssio, et pulchritúdo in conspéctu ejus: * sanctimónia et magnificéntia in sanctificatióne ejus.
verses.eng: 95:6 Praise and beauty are before him: * holiness and majesty in his sanctuary.

verses.lat: 95:7 Afférte Dómino, pátriæ géntium, afférte Dómino glóriam et honórem: * afférte Dómino glóriam nómini ejus.
verses.eng: 95:7 Bring ye to the Lord, O ye kindreds of the Gentiles, bring ye to the Lord glory and honour: * bring to the Lord glory unto his name.

verses.lat: 95:8 Tóllite hóstias, et introíte in átria ejus: * adoráte Dóminum in átrio sancto ejus.
verses.eng: 95:8 Bring up sacrifices, and come into his courts: * adore ye the Lord in his holy court.

verses.lat: 95:9 Commoveátur a fácie ejus univérsa terra: * dícite in géntibus quia Dóminus regnávit.
verses.eng: 95:9 Let all the earth be moved at his presence. * Say ye among the Gentiles, the Lord hath reigned.

verses.lat: 95:10 Étenim corréxit orbem terræ qui non commovébitur: * judicábit pópulos in æquitáte.
verses.eng: 95:10 For he hath corrected the world, which shall not be moved: * he will judge the people with justice.

verses.lat: 95:11 Læténtur cæli, et exsúltet terra: commoveátur mare, et plenitúdo ejus: * gaudébunt campi, et ómnia quæ in eis sunt.
verses.eng: 95:11 Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad, let the sea be moved, and the fulness thereof: * the fields and all things that are in them shall be joyful.

verses.lat: 95:12 Tunc exsultábunt ómnia ligna silvárum a fácie Dómini, quia venit: * quóniam venit judicáre terram.
verses.eng: 95:12 Then shall all the trees of the woods rejoice before the face of the Lord, because he cometh: * because he cometh to judge the earth.

verses.lat: 95:13 Judicábit orbem terræ in æquitáte, * et pópulos in veritáte sua.
verses.eng: 95:13 He shall judge the world with justice, * and the people with his truth.

laudes.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.lat: Cantáte * Dómino et benedícite nómini ejus.
laudes.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Sing ye * to the Lord and bless his name.

laudes.psalm2.label: Psalmus 42
laudes.psalm2.antiphonEng: The salvation of my countenance * and my God.

verses.lat: 42:1 Júdica me, Deus, et discérne causam meam de gente non sancta, * ab hómine iníquo, et dolóso érue me.
verses.eng: 42:1 Judge me, O God, and distinguish my cause from the nation that is not holy: * deliver me from the unjust and deceitful man.

verses.lat: 42:2 Quia tu es, Deus, fortitúdo mea: * quare me repulísti? et quare tristis incédo, dum afflígit me inimícus?
verses.eng: 42:2 For thou art God my strength: * why hast thou cast me off? and why do I go sorrowful whilst the enemy afflicteth me?

verses.lat: 42:3 Emítte lucem tuam et veritátem tuam: * ipsa me deduxérunt, et adduxérunt in montem sanctum tuum, et in tabernácula tua.
verses.eng: 42:3 Send forth thy light and thy truth: * they have conducted me, and brought me unto thy holy hill, and into thy tabernacles.

verses.lat: 42:4 Et introíbo ad altáre Dei: * ad Deum, qui lætíficat juventútem meam.
verses.eng: 42:4 And I will go in to the altar of God: * to God who giveth joy to my youth.

verses.lat: 42:5 Confitébor tibi in cíthara, Deus, Deus meus: * quare tristis es, ánima mea? et quare contúrbas me?
verses.eng: 42:5 To thee, O God my God, I will give praise upon the harp: * why art thou sad, O my soul? and why dost thou disquiet me?

verses.lat: 42:6 Spera in Deo, quóniam adhuc confitébor illi: * salutáre vultus mei, et Deus meus.
verses.eng: 42:6 Hope in God, for I will still give praise to him: * the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

laudes.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm2.eng: The salvation of my countenance * and my God.

laudes.psalm3.label: Psalmus 66
laudes.psalm3.antiphonLat: Illúmina, Dómine, * vultum tuum super nos.
laudes.psalm3.antiphonEng: May the Lord shine the light * of his countenance upon us.

verses.lat: 66:2 Deus misereátur nostri, et benedícat nobis: * illúminet vultum suum super nos, et misereátur nostri.
verses.eng: 66:2 May God have mercy on us, and bless us: * may he cause the light of his countenance to shine upon us, and may he have mercy on us.

verses.lat: 66:3 Ut cognoscámus in terra viam tuam, * in ómnibus géntibus salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: 66:3 That we may know thy way upon earth: * thy salvation in all nations.

verses.lat: 66:4 Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus: * confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes.
verses.eng: 66:4 Let people confess to thee, O God: * let all people give praise to thee.

verses.lat: 66:5 Læténtur et exsúltent gentes: * quóniam júdicas pópulos in æquitáte, et gentes in terra dírigis.
verses.eng: 66:5 Let the nations be glad and rejoice: * for thou judgest the people with justice, and directest the nations upon earth.

verses.lat: 66:6 Confiteántur tibi pópuli, Deus, confiteántur tibi pópuli omnes: * (7a) terra dedit fructum suum.
verses.eng: 66:6 Let the people, O God, confess to thee: * (7a) let all the people give praise to thee: the earth hath yielded her fruit.

verses.lat: 66:7b Benedícat nos Deus, Deus noster, (8) benedícat nos Deus: * et métuant eum omnes fines terræ.
verses.eng: 66:7b May God, our God bless us, (8) may God bless us: * and all the ends of the earth fear him.

laudes.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.lat: Illúmina, Dómine, * vultum tuum super nos.
laudes.antiphon.psalm3.eng: May the Lord shine the light * of his countenance upon us.

laudes.canticle1.label: Canticum 212
laudes.canticle1.antiphonLat: Exaltáte * Regem sæculórum in opéribus vestris.
laudes.canticle1.antiphonEng: Give ye glory to him * in your works.

verses.lat: (Canticum Tobiæ * Tob. 13:1-11)
verses.eng: (Canticle of_Tobias * Tob. 13:1-11)

verses.lat: 13:1 Magnus es, Dómine, in ætérnum, * et in ómnia sǽcula regnum tuum:
verses.eng: 13:1 Thou art great, O Lord, for ever, * and thy kingdom is unto all ages:

verses.lat: 13:2 Quóniam tu flagéllas, et salvas: dedúcis ad ínferos, et redúcis: * et non est qui effúgiat manum tuam.
verses.eng: 13:2 For thou scourgest, and thou savest: thou leadest down to hell, and bringest up again: * and there is none that can escape thy hand.

verses.lat: 13:3 Confitémini Dómino, fílii Israël, * et in conspéctu géntium laudáte eum:
verses.eng: 13:3 Give glory to the Lord, ye children of Israel, * and praise him in the sight of the Gentiles:

verses.lat: 13:4 Quóniam ídeo dispérsit vos inter gentes, quæ ignórant eum, * ut vos enarrétis mirabília ejus,
verses.eng: 13:4 Because he hath therefore scattered you among the Gentiles, who know not him, * that you may declare his wonderful works,

verses.lat: 13:5 Et faciátis scire eos, * quia non est álius Deus omnípotens præter eum.
verses.eng: 13:5 And make them know * that there is no other almighty God besides him.

verses.lat: 13:6 Ipse castigávit nos propter iniquitátes nostras: * et ipse salvábit nos propter misericórdiam suam.
verses.eng: 13:6 He hath chastised us for our iniquities: * and he will save us for his own mercy.

verses.lat: 13:7 Aspícite ergo quæ fecit nobíscum, et cum timóre et tremóre confitémini illi: * Regémque sæculórum exaltáte in opéribus vestris.
verses.eng: 13:7 See then what he hath done with us, and with fear and trembling give ye glory to him: * and extol the eternal King of worlds in your works.

verses.lat: 13:8 Ego autem in terra captivitátis meæ confitébor illi: * quóniam osténdit majestátem suam in gentem peccatrícem.
verses.eng: 13:8 As for me, I will praise him in the land of my captivity: * because he hath shewn his majesty toward a sinful nation.

verses.lat: 13:9 Convertímini ítaque, peccatóres, et fácite justítiam coram Deo, * credéntes quod fáciat vobíscum misericórdiam suam:
verses.eng: 13:9 Be converted therefore, ye sinners, and do justice before God, * believing that he will shew his mercy to you.

verses.lat: 13:10 Ego autem, et ánima mea * in eo lætábimur.
verses.eng: 13:10 And I and my soul * will rejoice in him.

verses.lat: 13:11 Benedícite Dóminum, omnes elécti ejus: * ágite dies lætítiæ, et confitémini illi.
verses.eng: 13:11 Bless ye the Lord, all his elect, * keep days of joy, and give glory to him.

laudes.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Exaltáte * Regem sæculórum in opéribus vestris.
laudes.antiphon.psalm4.eng: Give ye glory to him * in your works.

laudes.psalm4.label: Psalmus 134
laudes.psalm4.antiphonLat: Laudáte * nomen Dómini, qui statis in domo Dómini.
laudes.psalm4.antiphonEng: Praise * the name of the Lord, ye who stand in the house of the Lord.

verses.lat: 134:1 Laudáte nomen Dómini, * laudáte, servi, Dóminum.
verses.eng: 134:1 Praise ye the name of the Lord: * O you his servants, praise the Lord:

verses.lat: 134:2 Qui statis in domo Dómini, * in átriis domus Dei nostri.
verses.eng: 134:2 You that stand in the house of the Lord, * in the courts of the house of our God.

verses.lat: 134:3 Laudáte Dóminum, quia bonus Dóminus: * psállite nómini ejus, quóniam suáve.
verses.eng: 134:3 Praise ye the Lord, for the Lord is good: * sing ye to his name, for it is sweet.

verses.lat: 134:4 Quóniam Jacob elégit sibi Dóminus, * Israël in possessiónem sibi.
verses.eng: 134:4 For the Lord hath chosen Jacob unto himself: * Israel for his own possession.

verses.lat: 134:5 Quia ego cognóvi quod magnus est Dóminus, * et Deus noster præ ómnibus diis.
verses.eng: 134:5 For I have known that the Lord is great, * and our God is above all gods.

verses.lat: 134:6 Ómnia quæcúmque vóluit, Dóminus fecit in cælo, et in terra, * in mari, et in ómnibus abýssis.
verses.eng: 134:6 Whatsoever the Lord pleased he hath done, in heaven, in earth, * in the sea, and in all the deeps.

verses.lat: 134:7 Edúcens nubes ab extrémo terræ: * fúlgura in plúviam fecit.
verses.eng: 134:7 He bringeth up clouds from the end of the earth: * he hath made lightnings for the rain.

verses.lat: 134:8 Qui prodúcit ventos de thesáuris suis: * qui percússit primogénita Ægýpti ab hómine usque ad pecus.
verses.eng: 134:8 He bringeth forth winds out of his stores: * He slew the firstborn of Egypt from man even unto beast.

verses.lat: 134:9 Et misit signa, et prodígia in médio tui, Ægýpte: * in Pharaónem, et in omnes servos ejus.
verses.eng: 134:9 He sent forth signs and wonders in the midst of thee, O Egypt: * upon Pharao, and upon all his servants.

verses.lat: 134:10 Qui percússit gentes multas: * et occídit reges fortes:
verses.eng: 134:10 He smote many nations, * and slew mighty kings:

verses.lat: 134:11 Sehon, regem Amorrhæórum, et Og, regem Basan, * et ómnia regna Chánaan.
verses.eng: 134:11 Sehon king of the Amorrhites, and Og king of Basan, * and all the kingdoms of Chanaan.

verses.lat: 134:12 Et dedit terram eórum hereditátem, * hereditátem Israël, pópulo suo.
verses.eng: 134:12 And gave their land for an inheritance, * for an inheritance to his people Israel.

verses.lat: 134:13 Dómine, nomen tuum in ætérnum: * Dómine, memoriále tuum in generatiónem et generatiónem.
verses.eng: 134:13 Thy name, O Lord, is for ever: * thy memorial, O Lord, unto all generations.

verses.lat: 134:14 Quia judicábit Dóminus pópulum suum: * et in servis suis deprecábitur.
verses.eng: 134:14 For the Lord will judge his people, * and will be entreated in favour of his servants.

verses.lat: 134:15 Simulácra géntium argéntum, et aurum, * ópera mánuum hóminum.
verses.eng: 134:15 The idols of the Gentiles are silver and gold, * the works of men’s hands.

verses.lat: 134:16 Os habent, et non loquéntur: * óculos habent, et non vidébunt.
verses.eng: 134:16 They have a mouth, but they speak not: * they have eyes, but they see not.

verses.lat: 134:17 Aures habent, et non áudient: * neque enim est spíritus in ore ipsórum.
verses.eng: 134:17 They have ears, but they hear not: * neither is there any breath in their mouths.

verses.lat: 134:18 Símiles illis fiant qui fáciunt ea: * et omnes qui confídunt in eis.
verses.eng: 134:18 Let them that make them be like to them: * and every one that trusteth in them.

verses.lat: 134:19 Domus Israël, benedícite Dómino: * domus Aaron, benedícite Dómino.
verses.eng: 134:19 Bless the Lord, O house of Israel: * bless the Lord, O house of Aaron.

verses.lat: 134:20 Domus Levi, benedícite Dómino: * qui timétis Dóminum, benedícite Dómino.
verses.eng: 134:20 Bless the Lord, O house of Levi: * you that fear the Lord, bless the Lord.

verses.lat: 134:21 Benedíctus Dóminus ex Sion, * qui hábitat in Jerúsalem.
verses.eng: 134:21 Blessed be the Lord out of Sion, * who dwelleth in Jerusalem.

laudes.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Laudáte * nomen Dómini, qui statis in domo Dómini.
laudes.antiphon.psalm5.eng: Praise * the name of the Lord, ye who stand in the house of the Lord.

vesperae.capitulum.label: Capitulum (2 Cor 1:3-4)
vesperae.capitulum.lat: Benedíctus Deus, et Pater Dómini nostri Jesu Christi, Pater misericordiárum, et Deus totíus consolatiónis, qui consolátur nos in omni tribulatióne nostra.
vesperae.capitulum.eng: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort, who comforteth us in all our tribulation.

capitulum_laudes.label: Capitulum (Rom 13:12-13)
capitulum_laudes.lat: Nox præcéssit, dies autem appropinquávit. Abiciámus ergo ópera tenebrárum, et induámur arma lucis. Sicut in die honéste ambulémus.
capitulum_laudes.eng: The night is passed, and the day is at hand. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light. Let us walk honestly, as in the day.

responsory_vespera_1.label: Responsorium Breve
responsory_vespera_1.lat:
R.br. Benedícam Dóminum * In omni témpore.
R. Benedícam Dóminum * In omni témpore.
V. Semper laus ejus in ore meo.
R. In omni témpore.
&Gloria
R. Benedícam Dóminum * In omni témpore.
responsory_vespera_1.eng:
R.br. I will bless the Lord * at all times.
R. I will bless the Lord * at all times.
V. His praise shall be always in my mouth.
R. At all times
&Gloria
R. I will bless the Lord * at all times.

versum_tertia.label: Versiculus
versum_tertia.lat: ℣. Adjútor meus, esto, ne derelínquas me.
versum_tertia.eng: ℣. Be Thou my helper, forsake me not.
versum_tertia.latR: ℟. Neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
versum_tertia.engR: ℟. Do not Thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

versum_sexta.label: Versiculus
versum_sexta.lat: ℣. Dóminus regit me, et nihil mihi déerit.
versum_sexta.eng: ℣. The Lord ruleth me: and I shall want nothing.
versum_sexta.latR: ℟. In loco páscuæ ibi me collocávit.
versum_sexta.engR: ℟. He hath set me in a place of pasture.

versum_nona.label: Versiculus
versum_nona.lat: ℣. Ab occúltis meis munda me, Dómine.
versum_nona.eng: ℣. From my secret ones cleanse me, O Lord.
versum_nona.latR: ℟. Et ab aliénis parce servo tuo.
versum_nona.engR: ℟. And from those of others spare Thy servant.

ant_1.label: Antíphona
ant_1.eng: Overthrow, O Lord, * them that fight against me.

ant_2.label: Antíphona
ant_2.lat: Noli æmulári * in eo qui prosperátur et facit iniquitátem.
ant_2.eng: Envy not * the man who prospereth in his way; the man who doth unjust things.

ant_3.label: Antíphona
ant_3.lat: Ne in ira tua * corrípias me, Dómine.
ant_3.eng: O Lord, * do not chastise me in thy wrath.

nocturn_1_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn I
nocturn_1_versum.eng: ℣. And my tongue shall meditate thy justice.
nocturn_1_versum.engR: ℟. Thy praise all the day long, O Lord.

nocturn_2_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn II
nocturn_2_versum.lat: ℣. Exspécta Dóminum, et custódi viam ejus.
nocturn_2_versum.eng: ℣. Expect the Lord and keep his way.
nocturn_2_versum.latR: ℟. Exaltábit te, ut hereditáte cápias terram.
nocturn_2_versum.engR: ℟. He will exalt thee to inherit the land.

nocturn_3_versum.label: Versicle after Nocturn III
nocturn_3_versum.lat: ℣. Deus, ne síleas a me, remítte mihi.
nocturn_3_versum.eng: ℣. O Lord, be not thou silent, forgive me.
nocturn_3_versum.latR: ℟. Quóniam íncola ego sum apud te et peregrínus.
nocturn_3_versum.engR: ℟. For I am a stranger with thee, and a sojourner.

verses.lat: Dixi: Custódiam vias meas, ut non delínquam in lingua mea.
verses.eng: I said: I will take heed to my ways: that I sin not with my tongue.

verses.lat: Pósui ori meo custódiam, cum consísteret peccátor advérsum me.
verses.eng: I set a guard to my mouth, when the sinner stood against me.

verses.lat: Obmútui et humiliátus sum, et sílui a bonis, et dolor meus renovátus est.
verses.eng: I was dumb, and was humbled, and kept silence from good things: and my sorrow was renewed.

verses.lat: Concáluit cor meum intra me, et in meditatióne mea exardéscet ignis.
verses.eng: My heart grew hot within me: and in my meditation a fire shall flame out.

verses.lat: Locútus sum in lingua mea: Notum fac mihi, Dómine, finem meum.
verses.eng: I spoke with my tongue: O Lord, make me know my end.

verses.lat: Et númerum diérum meórum quis est, ut sciam quid desit mihi.
verses.eng: And what is the number of my days: that I may know what is wanting to me.

verses.lat: Ecce mensurábiles posuísti dies meos, et substántia mea tamquam níhilum ante te.
verses.eng: Behold, Thou hast made my days measurable: and my substance is as nothing before Thee.

verses.lat: Verúmtamen univérsa vánitas, omnis homo vivens.
verses.eng: And indeed all things are vanity: every man living.

verses.lat: Verúmtamen in imágine pertránsit homo; sed et frustra conturbátur.
verses.eng: Surely man passeth as an image: yea, and he is disquieted in vain.

verses.lat: Thesaurízat, et ignórat cui congregábit ea.
verses.eng: He storeth up: and he knoweth not for whom he shall gather these things.

verses.lat: Et nunc quæ est exspectátio mea? Nonne Dóminus? Et substántia mea apud te est.
verses.eng: And now what is my hope? Is it not the Lord? And my substance is with Thee.

verses.lat: Ab ómnibus iniquitátibus meis érue me; oppróbrium insipiénti dedísti me.
verses.eng: Deliver Thou me from all my iniquities: Thou hast made me a reproach to the fool.

verses.lat: Obmútui, et non apérui os meum, quóniam tu fecísti.
verses.eng: I was dumb, and I opened not my mouth, because Thou hast done it.

verses.lat: Amóve a me plagas tuas.
verses.eng: Remove Thy scourges from me.

verses.lat: A fortitúdine manus tuæ ego deféci in increpatiónibus; propter iniquitátem corripuísti hóminem.
verses.eng: The strength of Thy hand hath made me faint in rebukes: Thou hast corrected man for iniquity.

verses.lat: Et tabéscere fecísti sicut aráneam ánimam ejus; verúmtamen vane conturbátur omnis homo.
verses.eng: And Thou hast made his soul to waste away like a spider: surely in vain is any man disquieted.

verses.lat: Exáudi oratiónem meam, Dómine, et deprecatiónem meam; áuribus pércipe lácrimas meas.
verses.eng: Hear my prayer, O Lord, and my supplication: give ear to my tears.

verses.lat: Ne síleas, quóniam ádvena ego sum apud te, et peregrínus, sicut omnes patres mei.
verses.eng: Be not silent: for I am a stranger with Thee, and a sojourner as all my fathers were.

verses.lat: Remítte mihi, ut refrígerer priúsquam ábeam, et ámplius non ero.
verses.eng: O forgive me, that I may be refreshed, before I go hence, and be no more.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Exspéctans exspectávi Dóminum, et inténdit mihi.
verses.eng: With expectation I have waited for the Lord, and He was attentive to me.

verses.lat: Et exaudívit preces meas, et edúxit me de lacu misériæ et de luto fæcis.
verses.eng: And He heard my prayers, and brought me out of the pit of misery and the mire of dregs.

verses.lat: Et státuit super petram pedes meos, et diréxit gressus meos.
verses.eng: And He set my feet upon a rock, and directed my steps.

verses.lat: Et immísit in os meum cánticum novum, carmen Deo nostro.
verses.eng: And He put a new canticle into my mouth, a song to our God.

verses.lat: Vidébunt multi et timébunt, et sperábunt in Dómino.
verses.eng: Many shall see, and shall fear: and they shall hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: Beátus vir cujus est nomen Dómini spes ejus, et non respéxit in vanitátes et insánias falsas.
verses.eng: Blessed is the man whose trust is in the name of the Lord, and who hath not had regard to vanities and lying follies.

verses.lat: Multa fecísti tu, Dómine Deus meus, mirabília tua; et cogitatiónibus tuis non est qui símilis sit tibi.
verses.eng: Thou hast done many wonderful things, O Lord my God: and in Thy thoughts there is no one like to Thee.

verses.lat: Annuntiávi et locútus sum; multiplicáti sunt super númerum.
verses.eng: I have declared and I have spoken: they are multiplied above number.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium et oblatiónem noluísti; aures autem perfecísti mihi.
verses.eng: Sacrifice and oblation Thou didst not desire: but Thou hast pierced ears for me.

verses.lat: Holocáustum et pro peccáto non postulásti; tunc dixi: Ecce vénio.
verses.eng: Burnt offering and sin offering Thou didst not require: then said I: Behold I come.

verses.lat: In cápite libri scriptum est de me, ut fácerem voluntátem tuam; Deus meus, vólui, et legem tuam in médio cordis mei.
verses.eng: In the head of the book it is written of me that I should do Thy will: O my God, I have desired it, and Thy law in the midst of my heart.

verses.lat: Annuntiávi justítiam tuam in ecclésia magna; ecce lábia mea non prohibébo: Dómine, tu scisti.
verses.eng: I have declared Thy justice in a great church: lo, I will not restrain my lips: O Lord, Thou knowest it.

verses.lat: Justítiam tuam non abscóndi in corde meo; veritátem tuam et salutáre tuum dixi.
verses.eng: I have not hid Thy justice within my heart: I have declared Thy truth and Thy salvation.

verses.lat: Non abscóndi misericórdiam tuam et veritátem tuam a concílio multo.
verses.eng: I have not concealed Thy mercy and Thy truth from a great council.

verses.lat: Tu autem, Dómine, ne longe fácias miseratiónes tuas a me; misericórdia tua et véritas tua semper suscepérunt me.
verses.eng: Withhold not Thou, O Lord, Thy tender mercies from me: Thy mercy and Thy truth have always upheld me.

verses.lat: Quóniam circumdedérunt me mala quorum non est númerus; comprehendérunt me iniquitátes meæ, et non pótui ut vidérem.
verses.eng: For evils without number have surrounded me: my iniquities have overtaken me, and I was not able to see.

verses.lat: Multiplicátæ sunt super capíllos cápitis mei, et cor meum derelíquit me.
verses.eng: They are multiplied above the hairs of my head: and my heart hath forsaken me.

verses.lat: Compláceat tibi, Dómine, ut éruas me; Dómine, ad adjuvándum me réspice.
verses.eng: Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: look down, O Lord, to help me.

verses.lat: Confundántur et revereántur simul, qui quǽrunt ánimam meam, ut áuferant eam.
verses.eng: Let them be confounded and ashamed together, that seek after my soul to take it away.

verses.lat: Convertántur retrórsum et revereántur, qui volunt mihi mala.
verses.eng: Let them be turned backward and be ashamed, that desire evils to me.

verses.lat: Ferant conféstim confusiónem suam, qui dicunt mihi: Euge, euge.
verses.eng: Let them immediately bear their confusion, that say to me: 'Tis well, 'tis well.

verses.lat: Exsúltent et læténtur super te omnes quæréntes te, et dicant semper: Magnificétur Dóminus, qui díligunt salutáre tuum.
verses.eng: Let all that seek Thee rejoice and be glad in Thee: and let such as love Thy salvation say always: The Lord be magnified.

verses.lat: Ego autem mendícus sum et pauper; Dóminus sollícitus est mei.
verses.eng: But I am a beggar and poor: the Lord is careful for me.

verses.lat: Adjútor meus et protéctor meus tu es; Deus meus, ne tardáveris.
verses.eng: Thou art my helper and my protector: O my God, be not slack.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Deus, áuribus nostris audívimus; patres nostri annuntiavérunt nobis.
verses.eng: O God, we have heard with our ears: our fathers have declared to us.

verses.lat: Opus quod operátus es in diébus eórum, et in diébus antíquis.
verses.eng: The work Thou hast wrought in their days, and in the days of old.

verses.lat: Manus tua gentes dispérdidit, et plantásti eos; afflixísti pópulos, et expulísti eos.
verses.eng: Thy hand destroyed the Gentiles, and Thou plantedst them: Thou didst afflict the people, and cast them out.

verses.lat: Nec enim in gládio suo possedérunt terram, et brácchium eórum non salvávit eos.
verses.eng: For they got not the possession of the land by their own sword: neither did their own arm save them.

verses.lat: Sed déxtera tua et brácchium tuum, et illuminátio vultus tui, quóniam complacuísti in eis.
verses.eng: But Thy right hand and Thy arm, and the light of Thy countenance: because Thou wast pleased with them.

verses.lat: Tu es ipse Rex meus et Deus meus, qui mandas salútes Jacob.
verses.eng: Thou art Thyself my King and my God, who commandest the saving of Jacob.

verses.lat: In te inimícos nostros ventilábimus cornu, et in nómine tuo spernémus insurgéntes in nobis.
verses.eng: Through Thee we will push down our enemies with the horn: and through Thy name we will despise them that rise up against us.

verses.lat: Non enim in arcu meo sperábo, et gládius meus non salvábit me.
verses.eng: For I will not trust in my bow: neither shall my sword save me.

verses.lat: Salvásti enim nos de affligéntibus nos, et odiéntes nos confudísti.
verses.eng: But Thou hast saved us from them that afflict us: and hast put them to shame that hate us.

verses.lat: In Deo laudábimur tota die, et in nómine tuo confitébimur in sǽculum.
verses.eng: In God shall we glory all the day long: and in Thy name we will give praise for ever.

verses.lat: Nunc autem repulísti et confudísti nos, et non egrediéris, Deus, in virtútibus nostris.
verses.eng: But now Thou hast cast us off, and put us to shame: and Thou, O God, wilt not go out with our armies.

verses.lat: Avertísti nos retrórsum post inimícos nostros, et qui odérunt nos diripiébant sibi.
verses.eng: Thou hast made us turn our back to our enemies: and they that hated us plundered for themselves.

verses.lat: Dedísti nos tamquam oves escárum, et in géntibus dispersísti nos.
verses.eng: Thou hast given us up like sheep of slaughter: and hast scattered us among the nations.

verses.lat: Vendidísti pópulum tuum sine prétio, et non fuit multitúdo in commutatiónibus eórum.
verses.eng: Thou hast sold Thy people for no price: and there was no reckoning in the exchange of them.

verses.lat: Posuísti nos oppróbrium vicínis nostris, subsannatiónem et derísum his qui sunt in circúitu nostro.
verses.eng: Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours, a scoff and derision to them that are round about us.

verses.lat: Posuísti nos in similitúdinem géntibus, commoratiónem cápitis in pópulis.
verses.eng: Thou hast made us a byword among the Gentiles: a shaking of the head among the people.

verses.lat: Tota die verecúndia mea contra me est, et confúsio faciéi meæ coopéruit me.
verses.eng: All the day long my shame is before me: and the confusion of my face hath covered me.

verses.lat: A voce exprobrántis et obloquéntis, a fácie inimíci et persequéntis.
verses.eng: At the voice of him that reproacheth and detracteth me: at the face of the enemy and persecutor.

verses.lat: Hæc ómnia venérunt super nos; nec oblíti sumus te, et iníque non égimus in testaménto tuo.
verses.eng: All these things have come upon us, yet we have not forgotten Thee: and we have not done wickedly in Thy covenant.

verses.lat: Et non recéssit retro cor nostrum; et declinésti sémitas nostras a via tua.
verses.eng: And our heart hath not turned back: neither hast Thou turned aside our steps from Thy way.

verses.lat: Quóniam humiliásti nos in loco afflictiónis, et coopéruit nos umbra mortis.
verses.eng: For Thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction: and the shadow of death hath covered us.

verses.lat: Si oblíti sumus nomen Dei nostri, et si expándimus manus nostras ad deum aliénum:
verses.eng: If we have forgotten the name of our God, and if we have spread forth our hands to a strange god:

verses.lat: Nonne Deus requíret ista? Ipse enim novit abscóndita cordis.
verses.eng: Shall not God search out these things? For He knoweth the secrets of the heart.

verses.lat: Quóniam propter te mortificámur tota die; æstimáti sumus sicut oves occisiónis.
verses.eng: Because for Thy sake we are killed all the day long: we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

verses.lat: Exsúrge, quare obdórmis, Dómine? Exsúrge, et ne repéllas in finem.
verses.eng: Arise, why sleepest Thou, O Lord? Arise, and cast us not off to the end.

verses.lat: Quare fáciem tuam avértis, oblivísceris inópiæ nostræ et tribulatiónis nostræ?
verses.eng: Why turnest Thou Thy face away, and forgettest our want and our trouble?

verses.lat: Quóniam humiliáta est in púlvere ánima nostra; conglutinátus est in terra venter noster.
verses.eng: For our soul is humbled down to the dust: our belly cleaveth to the earth.

verses.lat: Exsúrge, Dómine, ádjuva nos, et rédime nos propter nomen tuum.
verses.eng: Arise, O Lord, help us and redeem us for Thy name's sake.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Eructávit cor meum verbum bonum; dico ego ópera mea regi.
verses.eng: My heart hath uttered a good word: I speak my works to the King.

verses.lat: Lingua mea cálamus scribæ velóciter scribéntis.
verses.eng: My tongue is the pen of a scrivener that writeth swiftly.

verses.lat: Speciósus forma præ fíliis hóminum, diffúsa est grátia in lábiis tuis; proptérea benedíxit te Deus in ætérnum.
verses.eng: Thou art beautiful above the sons of men: grace is poured abroad in Thy lips: therefore hath God blessed Thee for ever.

verses.lat: Accíngere gládio tuo super femur tuum, potentíssime.
verses.eng: Gird Thy sword upon Thy thigh, O Thou most mighty.

verses.lat: Spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua inténde, próspere procéde, et regna.
verses.eng: With Thy comeliness and Thy beauty set out, proceed prosperously, and reign.

verses.lat: Propter veritátem et mansuetúdinem et justítiam; et dedúcet te mirabíliter déxtera tua.
verses.eng: Because of truth and meekness and justice: and Thy right hand shall conduct thee wonderfully.

verses.lat: Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ, pópuli sub te cadent, in corda inimicórum regis.
verses.eng: Thy arrows are sharp: under Thee shall people fall, into the hearts of the King's enemies.

verses.lat: Sedes tua, Deus, in sǽculum sǽculi; virga directiónis, virga regni tui.
verses.eng: Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of Thy kingdom is a sceptre of uprightness.

verses.lat: Dilexísti justítiam et odísti iniquitátem; proptérea unxit te Deus, Deus tuus, óleo lætítiæ præ consórtibus tuis.
verses.eng: Thou hast loved justice and hated iniquity: therefore God, Thy God, hath anointed Thee with the oil of gladness above Thy fellows.

verses.lat: Myrrha et gutta et cásia a vestiméntis tuis, a dómibus ebúrneis; ex quibus delectavérunt te fíliæ regum in honóre tuo.
verses.eng: Myrrh and stacte and cassia perfume Thy garments, from the ivory houses: out of which the daughters of kings have delighted Thee in Thy glory.

verses.lat: Ástitit regína a dextris tuis in vestítu deauráto, circúmdata varietáte.
verses.eng: The queen stood on Thy right hand, in gilded clothing, surrounded with variety.

verses.lat: Audi, fília, et vide, et inclína aurem tuam; et oblivíscere pópulum tuum et domum patris tui.
verses.eng: Hearken, O daughter, and see, and incline thy ear: and forget thy people and thy father's house.

verses.lat: Et concupíscet Rex decórem tuum, quóniam ipse est Dóminus Deus tuus, et adorábunt eum.
verses.eng: And the King shall greatly desire thy beauty: for He is the Lord thy God, and Him they shall adore.

verses.lat: Et fíliæ Tyri in munéribus vultum tuum deprecabúntur; omnes dívites plebis.
verses.eng: And the daughters of Tyre with gifts, yea, all the rich among the people, shall entreat thy countenance.

verses.lat: Omnis glória ejus fíliæ Regis ab intus, in fímbriis áureis, circúmamícta varietátibus.
verses.eng: All the glory of the King's daughter is within, in golden borders, clothed round about with varieties.

verses.lat: Adducéntur Regi vírgines post eam; próximæ ejus afferéntur tibi.
verses.eng: After her shall virgins be brought to the King: her neighbours shall be brought to Thee.

verses.lat: Afferéntur in lætítia et exsultatióne; adducéntur in templum Regis.
verses.eng: They shall be brought with gladness and rejoicing: they shall be brought into the temple of the King.

verses.lat: Pro pátribus tuis nati sunt tibi fílii; constítues eos príncipes super omnem terram.
verses.eng: Instead of thy fathers, sons are born to thee: thou shalt make them princes over all the earth.

verses.lat: Mémores erunt nóminis tui in omni generatióne et generatiónem.
verses.eng: They shall remember thy name throughout all generations.

verses.lat: Proptérea pópuli confitebúntur tibi in ætérnum, et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: Therefore shall people praise thee for ever: yea, for ever and ever.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Deus noster refúgium et virtus; adjútor in tribulatiónibus quæ invenérunt nos nimis.
verses.eng: Our God is our refuge and strength: a helper in troubles, which have found us exceedingly.

verses.lat: Proptérea non timébimus dum turbábitur terra, et transferéntur montes in cor maris.
verses.eng: Therefore we will not fear, when the earth shall be troubled, and the mountains shall be removed into the heart of the sea.

verses.lat: Sonuérunt et turbátæ sunt aquæ eórum; conturbáti sunt montes in fortitúdine ejus.
verses.eng: Their waters roared and were troubled: the mountains were troubled with his strength.

verses.lat: Flúminis ímpetus lætíficat civitátem Dei; sanctificávit tabernáculum suum Altíssimus.
verses.eng: The stream of the river maketh the city of God joyful: the Most High hath sanctified His own tabernacle.

verses.lat: Deus in médio ejus, non commovébitur; adjuvábit eam Deus mane dilúculo.
verses.eng: God is in the midst thereof, it shall not be moved: God will help it in the morning early.

verses.lat: Conturbátæ sunt gentes, et inclináta sunt regna; dedit vocem suam, mota est terra.
verses.eng: Nations were troubled, and kingdoms were bowed down: He uttered His voice, the earth trembled.

verses.lat: Dóminus virtútum nobíscum; suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: The Lord of armies is with us: the God of Jacob is our protector.

verses.lat: Veníte et vidéte ópera Dómini, quæ pósuit prodígia super terram.
verses.eng: Come and behold ye the works of the Lord: what wonders He hath done upon earth.

verses.lat: Áuferens bella usque ad finem terræ. Arcum cónteret et confrínget arma, et scuta combúret igni.
verses.eng: Making wars to cease even to the end of the earth. He shall destroy the bow, and break the weapons: and the shield He shall burn in the fire.

verses.lat: Vacáte et vidéte quóniam ego sum Deus; exaltábor in géntibus, et exaltábor in terra.
verses.eng: Be still and see that I am God: I will be exalted among the nations, and I will be exalted in the earth.

verses.lat: Dóminus virtútum nobíscum; suscéptor noster Deus Jacob.
verses.eng: The Lord of armies is with us: the God of Jacob is our protector.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Magnus Dóminus et laudábilis nimis, in civitáte Dei nostri, in monte sancto ejus.
verses.eng: Great is the Lord, and exceedingly to be praised, in the city of our God, in His holy mountain.

verses.lat: Fundátur exsultatióne univérsæ terræ mons Sion, látera aquilónis, cívitas Regis magni.
verses.eng: With the joy of the whole earth is mount Sion founded, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.

verses.lat: Deus in dómibus ejus cognoscétur, cum suscípiet eam.
verses.eng: In her houses shall God be known, when He shall protect her.

verses.lat: Quóniam ecce reges terræ congregáti sunt, convenérunt in unum.
verses.eng: For behold the kings of the earth assembled themselves: they gathered together.

verses.lat: Ipsi vidéntes sic admiráti sunt, conturbáti sunt, commóti sunt; tremor apprehéndit eos.
verses.eng: So they saw, and they wondered, they were troubled, they were moved: trembling took hold of them.

verses.lat: Ibi dolóres ut parturiéntis; in spíritu veheménti cónteres naves Tharsis.
verses.eng: There were pains as of a woman in labour: with a vehement wind Thou shalt break in pieces the ships of Tharsis.

verses.lat: Sicut audívimus, sic vídimus in civitáte Dómini virtútum, in civitáte Dei nostri; Deus fundávit eam in ætérnum.
verses.eng: As we have heard, so have we seen, in the city of the Lord of hosts, in the city of our God: God hath founded it for ever.

verses.lat: Suscépimus, Deus, misericórdiam tuam in médio templi tui.
verses.eng: We have received Thy mercy, O God, in the midst of Thy temple.

verses.lat: Secúndum nomen tuum, Deus, sic et laus tua in fines terræ; justítia plena est déxtera tua.
verses.eng: According to Thy name, O God, so also is Thy praise unto the ends of the earth: Thy right hand is full of justice.

verses.lat: Lætétur mons Sion, et exsúltent fíliæ Judæ, propter judícia tua, Dómine.
verses.eng: Let mount Sion rejoice, and the daughters of Juda be glad: because of Thy judgments, O Lord.

verses.lat: Circúmdate Sion et complectímini eam; narráte in túrribus ejus.
verses.eng: Surround Sion, and encompass her: tell ye in her towers.

verses.lat: Pónite corda vestra in virtúte ejus, et distribúite domos ejus, ut enarrétis in progénie áltera.
verses.eng: Set your hearts on her strength, and distribute her houses, that ye may relate it in another generation.

verses.lat: Quóniam hic est Deus, Deus noster in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi; ipse reget nos in sǽcula.
verses.eng: For this is God, our God unto eternity, and for ever and ever: He shall rule us for evermore.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Audíte hæc, omnes gentes; áuribus percípite, omnes qui habitátis orbem:
verses.eng: Hear these things, all ye nations: give ear, all ye inhabitants of the world.

verses.lat: Quique terrígenæ et fílii hóminum, simul in unum dives et pauper.
verses.eng: All you that are earthborn, and you sons of men: both rich and poor together.

verses.lat: Os meum loquétur sapiéntiam, et meditátio cordis mei prudéntiam.
verses.eng: My mouth shall speak wisdom: and the meditation of my heart understanding.

verses.lat: Inclinábo in parábolam aurem meam; apériam in psaltério propositiónem meam.
verses.eng: I will incline my ear to a parable: I will open my proposition on the psaltery.

verses.lat: Cur timébo in die mala? Iníquitas calcánei mei circúmdabit me.
verses.eng: Why shall I fear in the evil day? The iniquity of my heel shall encompass me.

verses.lat: Qui confídunt in virtúte sua, et in multitúdine divitiárum suárum gloriántur.
verses.eng: They that trust in their own strength, and glory in the multitude of their riches.

verses.lat: Frater non rédimit, rédimet homo; non dabit Deo placatiónem suam.
verses.eng: No brother can redeem, nor shall man redeem: he shall not give to God his ransom.

verses.lat: Et prétium redemptiónis ánimæ suæ; et laborábit in ætérnum, et vivet adhuc in finem.
verses.eng: Nor the price of the redemption of his soul: and shall labour for ever, and shall still live unto the end.

verses.lat: Non vidébit intéritum, cum víderit sapiéntes moriéntes; simul insípiens et stultus períbunt.
verses.eng: He shall not see destruction, when he shall see the wise dying: the senseless and the fool shall perish together.

verses.lat: Et relínquent aliénis divítias suas; et sepúlcra eórum domus illórum in ætérnum.
verses.eng: And they shall leave their riches to strangers: and their sepulchres shall be their houses for ever.

verses.lat: Tabernácula eórum in progénie et progénie; vocavérunt nómina sua in terris suis.
verses.eng: Their dwelling places to all generations: they have called their lands by their names.

verses.lat: Et homo, cum in honóre esset, non intéllexit; comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
verses.eng: And man when he was in honour did not understand: he is compared to senseless beasts, and is become like to them.

verses.lat: Hæc via illórum scándalum ipsis, et póstea in ore suo complacebúnt.
verses.eng: This way of theirs is a stumbling-block to them: and afterwards they shall delight in their mouth.

verses.lat: Sicut oves in inférno pósiti sunt; mors depáscet eos.
verses.eng: They are laid in hell like sheep: death shall feed upon them.

verses.lat: Et dominabúntur eórum justi in matutíno; et auxílium eórum veteráscet in inférno a glória eórum.
verses.eng: And the just shall have dominion over them in the morning: and their help shall decay in hell from their glory.

verses.lat: Verúmtamen Deus rédimet ánimam meam de manu ínferi, cum accéperit me.
verses.eng: But God will redeem my soul from the hand of hell, when He shall receive me.

verses.lat: Ne timúeris cum dives factus fúerit homo, et cum multiplicáta fúerit glória domus ejus.
verses.eng: Be not thou afraid, when a man shall be made rich: and when the glory of his house shall be increased.

verses.lat: Quóniam cum interíerit, non sumet ómnia; neque descéndet cum eo glória ejus.
verses.eng: For when he shall die he shall take nothing away: nor shall his glory descend with him.

verses.lat: Quia ánima ejus in vita ipsíus benedicétur; confitébitur tibi cum beneféceris ei.
verses.eng: For in his lifetime his soul will be blessed: and he will praise Thee when Thou shalt do well to him.

verses.lat: Introíbit usque in progénies patrum suórum, et usque in ætérnum non vidébit lumen.
verses.eng: He shall go in to the generations of his fathers: and he shall never see light.

verses.lat: Homo, cum in honóre esset, non intéllexit; comparátus est juméntis insipiéntibus, et símilis factus est illis.
verses.eng: Man when he was in honour did not understand: he hath been compared to senseless beasts, and made like to them.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Deus deórum, Dóminus locútus est, et vocávit terram, a solis ortu usque ad occásum.
verses.eng: The God of gods, the Lord hath spoken: and He hath called the earth, from the rising of the sun, to the going down thereof.

verses.lat: Ex Sion spécies decóris ejus.
verses.eng: Out of Sion the loveliness of His beauty.

verses.lat: Deus maniféste véniet; Deus noster, et non silébit.
verses.eng: God shall come manifestly: our God shall come, and shall not keep silence.

verses.lat: Ignis in conspéctu ejus exardéscet, et in circúitu ejus tempéstas válida.
verses.eng: A fire shall burn before Him: and a mighty tempest shall be round about Him.

verses.lat: Advocábit cælum desúrsum, et terram, discérnere pópulum suum.
verses.eng: He shall call heaven from above, and the earth, to judge His people.

verses.lat: Congregáte illi sanctos ejus, qui órdinant testaméntum ejus super sacrifícia.
verses.eng: Gather ye together His saints to Him: who set His covenant before sacrifices.

verses.lat: Et annuntiábunt cæli justítiam ejus, quóniam Deus judex est.
verses.eng: And the heavens shall declare His justice: for God is judge.

verses.lat: Audi, pópulus meus, et loquar; Israël, et testificábor tibi: Deus, Deus tuus ego sum.
verses.eng: Hear, O My people, and I will speak: O Israel, and I will testify to thee: I am God, thy God.

verses.lat: Non in sacrifíciis tuis árguam te; holocáusta autem tua in conspéctu meo sunt semper.
verses.eng: I will not reprove thee for thy sacrifices: and thy burnt offerings are always in My sight.

verses.lat: Non accípiam de domo tua vítulos, neque de grégibus tuis hircos.
verses.eng: I will not take calves out of thy house: nor he goats out of thy flocks.

verses.lat: Quóniam meæ sunt omnes feræ silvárum, juménta in móntibus et boves.
verses.eng: For all the beasts of the woods are Mine: the cattle on the hills, and the oxen.

verses.lat: Cognóvi ómnia volatília cæli, et pulchritúdo agri mecum est.
verses.eng: I know all the fowls of the air: and with Me is the beauty of the field.

verses.lat: Si esuríero, non dicam tibi; meus est enim orbis terræ et plenitúdo ejus.
verses.eng: If I should be hungry, I would not tell thee: for the world is Mine, and the fulness thereof.

verses.lat: Numquid manducábo carnes taurórum, aut sánguinem hircórum potábo?
verses.eng: Shall I eat the flesh of bullocks? Or shall I drink the blood of goats?

verses.lat: Ímmola Deo sacrifícium laudis, et redde Altíssimo vota tua.
verses.eng: Offer to God the sacrifice of praise: and pay thy vows to the Most High.

verses.lat: Et ínvoca me in die tribulatiónis; éruam te, et honorificábis me.
verses.eng: And call upon Me in the day of trouble: I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify Me.

verses.lat: Peccatóri autem dixit Deus: Quare tu enárras justítias meas, et assúmis testaméntum meum per os tuum?
verses.eng: But to the sinner God hath said: Why dost thou declare My justices, and take My covenant in thy mouth?

verses.lat: Tu vero odísti disciplínam, et projecísti sermónes meos retrórsum.
verses.eng: Seeing thou hast hated discipline: and hast cast My words behind thee.

verses.lat: Si vidébas furem, currébas cum eo, et cum adúlteris portiónem tuam ponébas.
verses.eng: If thou didst see a thief thou didst run with him: and with adulterers thou hast been a partaker.

verses.lat: Os tuum abundávit malítia, et lingua tua concinnábat dolos.
verses.eng: Thy mouth hath abounded with evil, and thy tongue framed deceits.

verses.lat: Sedens advérsus fratrem tuum loquebáris, et advérsus fílium matris tuæ ponébas scándalum.
verses.eng: Sitting thou didst speak against thy brother, and didst lay a scandal against thy mother's son.

verses.lat: Hæc fecísti, et tácui. Existimásti iníque quod ero tui símilis; árguam te, et státuam contra fáciem tuam.
verses.eng: These things hast thou done, and I was silent. Thou thoughtest unjustly that I should be like to thee: but I will reprove thee, and set before thy face.

verses.lat: Intellígite hæc, qui obliviscímini Deum; nequándo rápiat, et non sit qui erípiat.
verses.eng: Understand these things, you that forget God: lest He snatch you away, and there be none to deliver you.

verses.lat: Sacrifícium laudis honorificábit me; et illic iter quo osténdam illi salutáre Dei.
verses.eng: The sacrifice of praise shall glorify Me: and there is the way by which I will show him the salvation of God.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

verses.lat: Quid gloriáris in malítia, qui potens es in iniquitáte?
verses.eng: Why dost thou glory in malice, thou that art mighty in iniquity?

verses.lat: Tota die injustítiam cogitávit lingua tua; sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
verses.eng: All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.

verses.lat: Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem, iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
verses.eng: Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.

verses.lat: Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, lingua dolósa.
verses.eng: Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, O deceitful tongue.

verses.lat: Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem; evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo, et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: He will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.

verses.lat: Vidébunt justi et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt et dicent:
verses.eng: The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say:

verses.lat: Ecce homo qui non pósuit Deum adjutórem suum; sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum, et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
verses.eng: Behold the man that made not God his helper: but trusted in the abundance of his riches: and prevailed in his vanity.

verses.lat: Ego autem sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei; sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, have hoped in the mercy of God for ever and ever.

verses.lat: Confitébor tibi in sǽculum quia fecísti, et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
verses.eng: I will praise Thee for ever, because Thou hast done it: and I will wait on Thy name, for it is good in the sight of Thy saints.

verses.lat: Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
verses.eng: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

vesperae.psalm1.label: Psalmus 127
vesperae.psalm1.antiphonEng: Blessed are all * they that fear the Lord.

verses.lat: 127:1 Beáti, omnes, qui timent Dóminum, * qui ámbulant in viis ejus.
verses.eng: 127:1 Blessed are all they that fear the Lord: * that walk in his ways.

verses.lat: 127:2 Labóres mánuum tuárum quia manducábis: * beátus es, et bene tibi erit.
verses.eng: 127:2 For thou shalt eat the labours of thy hands: * blessed art thou, and it shall be well with thee.

verses.lat: 127:3a Uxor tua sicut vitis abúndans, * in latéribus domus tuæ.
verses.eng: 127:3a Thy wife as a fruitful vine, * on the sides of thy house.

verses.lat: 127:3b Fílii tui sicut novéllæ olivárum, * in circúitu mensæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 127:3b Thy children as olive plants, * round about thy table.

verses.lat: 127:4 Ecce, sic benedicétur homo, * qui timet Dóminum.
verses.eng: 127:4 Behold, thus shall the man be blessed * that feareth the Lord.

verses.lat: 127:5 Benedícat tibi Dóminus ex Sion: * et vídeas bona Jerúsalem ómnibus diébus vitæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 127:5 May the Lord bless thee out of Sion: * and mayst thou see the good things of Jerusalem all the days of thy life.

verses.lat: 127:6 Et vídeas fílios filiórum tuórum, * pacem super Israël.
verses.eng: 127:6 And mayst thou see thy children’s children, * peace upon Israel.

vesperae.psalm2.label: Psalmus 128
vesperae.psalm2.antiphonEng: Let them all be confounded * who hate Sion.

verses.lat: 128:1 Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea, * dicat nunc Israël.
verses.eng: 128:1 Often have they fought against me from my youth, * let Israel now say.

verses.lat: 128:2 Sæpe expugnavérunt me a juventúte mea: * étenim non potuérunt mihi.
verses.eng: 128:2 Often have they fought against me from my youth: * but they could not prevail over me.

verses.lat: 128:3 Supra dorsum meum fabricavérunt peccatóres: * prolongavérunt iniquitátem suam.
verses.eng: 128:3 The wicked have wrought upon my back: * they have lengthened their iniquity.

verses.lat: 128:4 Dóminus justus concídit cervíces peccatórum: * confundántur et convertántur retrórsum omnes, qui odérunt Sion.
verses.eng: 128:4 The Lord who is just will cut the necks of sinners: * let them all be confounded and turned back that hate Sion.

verses.lat: 128:6 Fiant sicut fænum tectórum: * quod priúsquam evellátur, exáruit:
verses.eng: 128:6 Let them be as grass upon the tops of houses: * which withereth before it be plucked up:

verses.lat: 128:7 De quo non implévit manum suam qui metit, * et sinum suum qui manípulos cólligit.
verses.eng: 128:7 Wherewith the mower filleth not his hand: * nor he that gathereth sheaves his bosom.

verses.lat: 128:8 Et non dixérunt qui præteríbant: Benedíctio Dómini super vos: * benedíximus vobis in nómine Dómini.
verses.eng: 128:8 And they that passed by have not said: The blessing of the Lord be upon you: * we have blessed you in the name of the Lord.

vesperae.psalm3.label: Psalmus 129
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonLat: De profúndis * clamávi ad te, Dómine.
vesperae.psalm3.antiphonEng: Out of the depths * I have cried to thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 129:1 De profúndis clamávi ad te, Dómine: * Dómine, exáudi vocem meam:
verses.eng: 129:1 Out of the depths I have cried to thee, O Lord: * Lord, hear my voice.

verses.lat: 129:2 Fiant aures tuæ intendéntes, * in vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
verses.eng: 129:2 Let thy ears be attentive * to the voice of my supplication.

verses.lat: 129:3 Si iniquitátes observáveris, Dómine: * Dómine, quis sustinébit?
verses.eng: 129:3 If thou, O Lord, wilt mark iniquities: * Lord, who shall stand it.

verses.lat: 129:4 Quia apud te propitiátio est: * et propter legem tuam sustínui te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 129:4 For with thee there is merciful forgiveness: * and by reason of thy law, I have waited for thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 129:5 Sustínuit ánima mea in verbo ejus: * sperávit ánima mea in Dómino.
verses.eng: 129:5 My soul hath relied on his word: * my soul hath hoped in the Lord.

verses.lat: 129:6 A custódia matutína usque ad noctem: * speret Israël in Dómino.
verses.eng: 129:6 From the morning watch even until night, * let Israel hope in the Lord.

verses.lat: 129:7 Quia apud Dóminum misericórdia: * et copiósa apud eum redémptio.
verses.eng: 129:7 Because with the Lord there is mercy: * and with him plentiful redemption.

verses.lat: 129:8 Et ipse rédimet Israël, * ex ómnibus iniquitátibus ejus.
verses.eng: 129:8 And he shall redeem Israel * from all his iniquities.

vesperae.psalm4.label: Psalmus 130
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonLat: Dómine, * non est exaltátum cor meum.
vesperae.psalm4.antiphonEng: O Lord * my heart is not exalted.

verses.lat: 130:1 Dómine, non est exaltátum cor meum: * neque eláti sunt óculi mei.
verses.eng: 130:1 O Lord, my heart is not exalted: * nor are my eyes lofty.

verses.lat: 130:1 Neque ambulávi in magnis: * neque in mirabílibus super me.
verses.eng: 130:1 Neither have I walked in great matters, * nor in wonderful things above me.

verses.lat: 130:2 Si non humíliter sentiébam: * sed exaltávi ánimam meam:
verses.eng: 130:2 If I was not humbly minded, * but exalted my soul:

verses.lat: 130:2 Sicut ablactátus est super matre sua, * ita retribútio in ánima mea.
verses.eng: 130:2 As a child that is weaned is towards his mother, * so reward in my soul.

verses.lat: 130:3 Speret Israël in Dómino, * ex hoc nunc et usque in sǽculum.
verses.eng: 130:3 Let Israel hope in the Lord, * from henceforth now and for ever.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm1.eng: Blessed are all * they that fear the Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm2.eng: Let them all be confounded * who hate Sion.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.lat: De profúndis * clamávi ad te, Dómine.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm3.eng: Out of the depths * I have cried to thee, O Lord.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.lat: Dómine, * non est exaltátum cor meum.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm4.eng: O Lord * my heart is not exalted.

vesperae.psalm5.label: Psalmus 131
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonLat: Elégit Dóminus * Sion in habitatiónem sibi.
vesperae.psalm5.antiphonEng: The Lord hath chosen * Sion for his dwelling.

verses.lat: 131:1 Meménto, Dómine, David, * et omnis mansuetúdinis ejus:
verses.eng: 131:1 Lord, remember David, * and all his meekness.

verses.lat: 131:2 Sicut jurávit Dómino, * votum vovit Deo Jacob:
verses.eng: 131:2 How he swore to the Lord, * he vowed a vow to the God of Jacob:

verses.lat: 131:3 Si introíero in tabernáculum domus meæ, * si ascéndero in lectum strati mei:
verses.eng: 131:3 If I shall enter into the tabernacle of my house: * if I shall go up into the bed wherein I lie:

verses.lat: 131:4 Si dédero somnum óculis meis, * et pálpebris meis dormitatiónem:
verses.eng: 131:4 If I shall give sleep to my eyes, * or slumber to my eyelids,

verses.lat: 131:5 Et réquiem tempóribus meis: donec invéniam locum Dómino, * tabernáculum Deo Jacob.
verses.eng: 131:5 Or rest to my temples: until I find out a place for the Lord, * a tabernacle for the God of Jacob.

verses.lat: 131:6 Ecce, audívimus eam in Éphrata: * invénimus eam in campis silvæ.
verses.eng: 131:6 Behold we have heard of it in Ephrata: * we have found it in the fields of the wood.

verses.lat: 131:7 Introíbimus in tabernáculum ejus: * adorábimus in loco, ubi stetérunt pedes ejus.
verses.eng: 131:7 We will go into his tabernacle: * we will adore in the place where his feet stood.

verses.lat: 131:8 Surge, Dómine, in réquiem tuam, * tu et arca sanctificatiónis tuæ.
verses.eng: 131:8 Arise, O Lord, into thy resting place: * thou and the ark, which thou hast sanctified.

verses.lat: 131:9 Sacerdótes tui induántur justítiam: * et sancti tui exsúltent.
verses.eng: 131:9 Let thy priests be clothed with justice: * and let thy saints rejoice.

verses.lat: 131:10 Propter David, servum tuum, * non avértas fáciem Christi tui.
verses.eng: 131:10 For thy servant David’s sake, * turn not away the face of thy anointed.

verses.lat: 131:11 Jurávit Dóminus David veritátem, et non frustrábitur eam: * De fructu ventris tui ponam super sedem tuam.
verses.eng: 131:11 The Lord hath sworn truth to David, and he will not make it void: * of the fruit of thy womb I will set upon thy throne.

verses.lat: 131:12 Si custodíerint fílii tui testaméntum meum, * et testimónia mea hæc, quæ docébo eos:
verses.eng: 131:12 If thy children will keep my covenant, * and these my testimonies which I shall teach them:

verses.lat: 131:12 Et fílii eórum usque in sǽculum, * sedébunt super sedem tuam.
verses.eng: 131:12 Their children also for evermore * shall sit upon thy throne.

verses.lat: 131:13 Quóniam elégit Dóminus Sion: * elégit eam in habitatiónem sibi.
verses.eng: 131:13 For the Lord hath chosen Sion: * he hath chosen it for his dwelling.

verses.lat: 131:14 Hæc réquies mea in sǽculum sǽculi: * hic habitábo quóniam elégi eam.
verses.eng: 131:14 This is my rest for ever and ever: * here will I dwell, for I have chosen it.

verses.lat: 131:15 Víduam ejus benedícens benedícam: * páuperes ejus saturábo pánibus.
verses.eng: 131:15 Blessing I will bless her widow: * I will satisfy her poor with bread.

verses.lat: 131:16 Sacerdótes ejus índuam salutári: * et sancti ejus exsultatióne exsultábunt.
verses.eng: 131:16 I will clothe her priests with salvation: * and her saints shall rejoice with exceeding great joy.

verses.lat: 131:17 Illuc prodúcam cornu David, * parávi lucérnam Christo meo.
verses.eng: 131:17 There will I bring forth a horn to David: * I have prepared a lamp for my anointed.

verses.lat: 131:18 Inimícos ejus índuam confusióne: * super ipsum autem efflorébit sanctificátio mea.
verses.eng: 131:18 His enemies I will clothe with confusion: * but upon him shall my sanctification flourish.

vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.label: Antíphona
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.lat: Elégit Dóminus * Sion in habitatiónem sibi.
vesperae.antiphon.psalm5.eng: The Lord hath chosen * Sion for his dwelling.

ant_prima.label: Antíphona
ant_prima.lat: Misericórdia tua, * Dómine, ante óculos meos: et complácui in veritáte tua.
ant_prima.eng: For thy mercy, * O Lord, is before my eyes; and I am well pleased with thy truth.

verses.lat: 25:1 Júdica me, Dómine, quóniam ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * et in Dómino sperans non infirmábor.
verses.eng: 25:1 Judge me, O Lord, for I have walked in my innocence: * and I have put my trust in the Lord, and shall not be weakened.

verses.lat: 25:2 Proba me, Dómine, et tenta me: * ure renes meos et cor meum.
verses.eng: 25:2 Prove me, O Lord, and try me; * burn my reins and my heart.

verses.lat: 25:3 Quóniam misericórdia tua ante óculos meos est: * et complácui in veritáte tua.
verses.eng: 25:3 For thy mercy is before my eyes; * and I am well pleased with thy truth.

verses.lat: 25:4 Non sedi cum concílio vanitátis: * et cum iníqua geréntibus non introíbo.
verses.eng: 25:4 I have not sat with the council of vanity: * neither will I go in with the doers of unjust things.

verses.lat: 25:5 Odívi ecclésiam malignántium: * et cum ímpiis non sedébo.
verses.eng: 25:5 I have hated the assembly of the malignant; * and with the wicked I will not sit.

verses.lat: 25:6 Lavábo inter innocéntes manus meas: * et circúmdabo altáre tuum, Dómine:
verses.eng: 25:6 I will wash my hands among the innocent; * and will compass thy altar, O Lord:

verses.lat: 25:7 Ut áudiam vocem laudis, * et enárrem univérsa mirabília tua.
verses.eng: 25:7 That I may hear the voice of thy praise: * and tell of all thy wondrous works.

verses.lat: 25:8 Dómine, diléxi decórem domus tuæ, * et locum habitatiónis glóriæ tuæ.
verses.eng: 25:8 I have loved, O Lord, the beauty of thy house; * and the place where thy glory dwelleth.

verses.lat: 25:9 Ne perdas cum ímpiis, Deus, ánimam meam, * et cum viris sánguinum vitam meam:
verses.eng: 25:9 Take not away my soul, O God, with the wicked: * nor my life with bloody men:

verses.lat: 25:10 In quorum mánibus iniquitátes sunt: * déxtera eórum repléta est munéribus.
verses.eng: 25:10 In whose hands are iniquities: * their right hand is filled with gifts.

verses.lat: 25:11 Ego autem in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum: * rédime me, et miserére mei.
verses.eng: 25:11 But as for me, I have walked in my innocence: * redeem me, and have mercy on me.

verses.lat: 25:12 Pes meus stetit in dirécto: * in ecclésiis benedícam te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 25:12 My foot hath stood in the direct way: * in the churches I will bless thee, O Lord.

verses.lat: 51:3 Quid gloriáris in malítia, * qui potens es in iniquitáte?
verses.eng: 51:3 Why dost thou glory in malice, * thou that art mighty in iniquity?

verses.lat: 51:4 Tota die injustítiam cogitávit lingua tua: * sicut novácula acúta fecísti dolum.
verses.eng: 51:4 All the day long thy tongue hath devised injustice: * as a sharp razor, thou hast wrought deceit.

verses.lat: 51:5 Dilexísti malítiam super benignitátem: * iniquitátem magis quam loqui æquitátem.
verses.eng: 51:5 Thou hast loved malice more than goodness: * and iniquity rather than to speak righteousness.

verses.lat: 51:6 Dilexísti ómnia verba præcipitatiónis, * lingua dolósa.
verses.eng: 51:6 Thou hast loved all the words of ruin, * O deceitful tongue.

verses.lat: 51:7 Proptérea Deus déstruet te in finem, * evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium.
verses.eng: 51:7 Therefore will God destroy thee for ever: * he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living.

verses.lat: 51:8 Vidébunt justi, et timébunt, et super eum ridébunt, et dicent: * Ecce homo, qui non pósuit Deum adjutórem suum:
verses.eng: 51:8 The just shall see and fear, and shall laugh at him, and say: * Behold the man that made not God his helper:

verses.lat: 51:9 Sed sperávit in multitúdine divitiárum suárum: * et præváluit in vanitáte sua.
verses.eng: 51:9 But trusted in the abundance of his riches: * and prevailed in his vanity.

verses.lat: 51:10 Ego autem, sicut olíva fructífera in domo Dei, * sperávi in misericórdia Dei in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi.
verses.eng: 51:10 But I, as a fruitful olive tree in the house of God, * have hoped in the mercy of God for ever, yea for ever and ever.

verses.lat: 51:11 Confitébor tibi in sǽculum, quia fecísti: * et exspectábo nomen tuum, quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum.
verses.eng: 51:11 I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it: * and I will wait on thy name, for it is good in the sight of thy saints.

verses.lat: 52:1 Dixit insípiens in corde suo: * Non est Deus.
verses.eng: 52:1 The fool said in his heart: * There is no God.

verses.lat: 52:2 Corrúpti sunt, et abominábiles facti sunt in iniquitátibus: * non est qui fáciat bonum.
verses.eng: 52:2 They are corrupted, and become abominable in iniquities: * there is none that doth good.

verses.lat: 52:3 Deus de cælo prospéxit super fílios hóminum: * ut vídeat si est intéllegens, aut requírens Deum.
verses.eng: 52:3 God looked down from heaven on the children of men: * to see if there were any that did understand, or did seek God.

verses.lat: 52:4 Omnes declinavérunt, simul inútiles facti sunt: * non est qui fáciat bonum, non est usque ad unum.
verses.eng: 52:4 All have gone aside, they are become unprofitable together, * there is none that doth good, no not one.

verses.lat: 52:5 Nonne scient omnes qui operántur iniquitátem, * qui dévorant plebem meam ut cibum panis?
verses.eng: 52:5 Shall not all the workers of iniquity know, * who eat up my people as they eat bread?

verses.lat: 52:6 Deum non invocavérunt: * illic trepidavérunt timóre, ubi non erat timor.
verses.eng: 52:6 They have not called upon God: * there have they trembled for fear, where there was no fear.

verses.lat: 52:6 Quóniam Deus dissipávit ossa eórum qui homínibus placent: * confúsi sunt, quóniam Deus sprevit eos.
verses.eng: 52:6 For God hath scattered the bones of them that please men: * they have been confounded, because God hath despised them.

verses.lat: 52:7 Quis dabit ex Sion salutáre Israël? * cum convérterit Deus captivitátem plebis suæ, exsultábit Jacob, et lætábitur Israël.
verses.eng: 52:7 Who will give out of Sion the salvation of Israel? * when God shall bring back the captivity of his people, Jacob shall rejoice, and Israel shall be glad.

ant_tertia.label: Antíphona
ant_tertia.lat: Deus ádjuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
ant_tertia.eng: For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

verses.lat: 53:3 Deus, in nómine tuo salvum me fac: * et in virtúte tua júdica me.
verses.eng: 53:3 Save me, O God, by thy name, * and judge me in thy strength.

verses.lat: 53:4 Deus, exáudi oratiónem meam: * áuribus pércipe verba oris mei.
verses.eng: 53:4 O God, hear my prayer: * give ear to the words of my mouth.

verses.lat: 53:5 Quóniam aliéni insurrexérunt advérsum me, et fortes quæsiérunt ánimam meam: * et non proposuérunt Deum ante conspéctum suum.
verses.eng: 53:5 For strangers have risen up against me; and the mighty have sought after my soul: * and they have not set God before their eyes.

verses.lat: 53:6 Ecce enim, Deus ádjuvat me: * et Dóminus suscéptor est ánimæ meæ.
verses.eng: 53:6 For behold God is my helper: * and the Lord is the protector of my soul.

verses.lat: 53:7 Avérte mala inimícis meis: * et in veritáte tua dispérde illos.
verses.eng: 53:7 Turn back the evils upon my enemies; * and cut them off in thy truth.

verses.lat: 53:8 Voluntárie sacrificábo tibi, * et confitébor nómini tuo, Dómine: quóniam bonum est:
verses.eng: 53:8 I will freely sacrifice to thee, * and will give praise, O God, to thy name: because it is good:

verses.lat: 53:9 Quóniam ex omni tribulatióne eripuísti me: * et super inimícos meos despéxit óculus meus.
verses.eng: 53:9 For thou hast delivered me out of all trouble: * and my eye hath looked down upon my enemies.

verses.lat: 54:2 Exáudi, Deus, oratiónem meam, et ne despéxeris deprecatiónem meam: * inténde mihi, et exáudi me.
verses.eng: 54:2 Hear, O God, my prayer, and despise not my supplication: * be attentive to me and hear me.

verses.lat: 54:3 Contristátus sum in exercitatióne mea: * et conturbátus sum a voce inimíci, et a tribulatióne peccatóris.
verses.eng: 54:3 I am grieved in my exercise; * and am troubled, at the voice of the enemy, and at the tribulation of the sinner.

verses.lat: 54:4 Quóniam declinavérunt in me iniquitátes: * et in ira molésti erant mihi.
verses.eng: 54:4 For they have cast iniquities upon me; * and in wrath they were troublesome to me.

verses.lat: 54:5 Cor meum conturbátum est in me: * et formído mortis cécidit super me.
verses.eng: 54:5 My heart is troubled within me: * and the fear of death is fallen upon me.

verses.lat: 54:6 Timor et tremor venérunt super me: * et contexérunt me ténebræ.
verses.eng: 54:6 Fear and trembling are come upon me: * and darkness hath covered me.

verses.lat: 54:7 Et dixi: Quis dabit mihi pennas sicut colúmbæ, * et volábo, et requiéscam?
verses.eng: 54:7 And I said: Who will give me wings like a dove, * and I will fly and be at rest?

verses.lat: 54:8 Ecce, elongávi fúgiens: * et mansi in solitúdine.
verses.eng: 54:8 Lo, I have gone far off flying away; * and I abode in the wilderness.

verses.lat: 54:9 Exspectábam eum, qui salvum me fecit * a pusillanimitáte spíritus et tempestáte.
verses.eng: 54:9 I waited for him that hath saved me * from pusillanimity of spirit, and a storm.

verses.lat: 54:10 Præcípita, Dómine, dívide linguas eórum: * quóniam vidi iniquitátem, et contradictiónem in civitáte.
verses.eng: 54:10 Cast down, O Lord, and divide their tongues; * for I have seen iniquity and contradiction in the city.

verses.lat: 54:11 Die ac nocte circúmdabit eam super muros ejus iníquitas: * et labor in médio ejus, et injustítia.
verses.eng: 54:11 Day and night shall iniquity surround it upon its walls: * and in the midst thereof are labour, and injustice.

verses.lat: 54:12 Et non defécit de platéis ejus * usúra, et dolus.
verses.eng: 54:12 And usury and deceit * have not departed from its streets.

verses.lat: 54:13 Quóniam si inimícus meus maledixísset mihi, * sustinuíssem útique.
verses.eng: 54:13 For if my enemy had reviled me, * I would verily have borne with it.

verses.lat: 54:13 Et si is, qui óderat me, super me magna locútus fuísset, * abscondíssem me fórsitan ab eo.
verses.eng: 54:13 And if he that hated me had spoken great things against me, * I would perhaps have hidden myself from him.

verses.lat: 54:14 Tu vero, homo unánimis: * dux meus, et notus meus:
verses.eng: 54:14 But thou a man of one mind, * my guide, and my familiar.

verses.lat: 54:15 Qui simul mecum dulces capiébas cibos: * in domo Dei ambulávimus cum consénsu.
verses.eng: 54:15 Who didst take sweetmeats together with me: * in the house of God we walked with consent.

verses.lat: 54:16 Véniat mors super illos: * et descéndant in inférnum vivéntes:
verses.eng: 54:16 Let death come upon them, * and let them go down alive into hell.

verses.lat: 54:16 Quóniam nequítiæ in habitáculis eórum: * in médio eórum.
verses.eng: 54:16 For there is wickedness in their dwellings: * in the midst of them.

verses.lat: 54:17 Ego autem ad Deum clamávi: * et Dóminus salvábit me.
verses.eng: 54:17 But I have cried to God: * and the Lord will save me.

verses.lat: 54:18 Véspere, et mane, et merídie narrábo et annuntiábo: * et exáudiet vocem meam.
verses.eng: 54:18 Evening and morning, and at noon I will speak and declare: * and he shall hear my voice.

verses.lat: 54:19 Rédimet in pace ánimam meam ab his, qui appropínquant mihi: * quóniam inter multos erant mecum.
verses.eng: 54:19 He shall redeem my soul in peace from them that draw near to me: * for among many they were with me.

verses.lat: 54:20 Exáudiet Deus, et humiliábit illos, * qui est ante sǽcula.
verses.eng: 54:20 God shall hear, * and the Eternal shall humble them.

verses.lat: 54:20 Non enim est illis commutátio, et non timuérunt Deum: * exténdit manum suam in retribuéndo.
verses.eng: 54:20 For there is no change with them, and they have not feared God: * he hath stretched forth his hand to repay.

verses.lat: 54:21 Contaminavérunt testaméntum ejus, divísi sunt ab ira vultus ejus: * et appropinquávit cor illíus.
verses.eng: 54:21 They have defiled his covenant, they are divided by the wrath of his countenance, * and his heart hath drawn near.

verses.lat: 54:22 Mollíti sunt sermónes ejus super óleum: * et ipsi sunt jácula.
verses.eng: 54:22 His words are smoother than oil, * and the same are darts.

verses.lat: 54:23 Jacta super Dóminum curam tuam, et ipse te enútriet: * non dabit in ætérnum fluctuatiónem justo.
verses.eng: 54:23 Cast thy care upon the Lord, and he shall sustain thee: * he shall not suffer the just to waver for ever.

verses.lat: 54:24 Tu vero, Deus, dedúces eos, * in púteum intéritus.
verses.eng: 54:24 But thou, O God, shalt bring them down * into the pit of destruction.

verses.lat: 54:24 Viri sánguinum, et dolósi non dimidiábunt dies suos: * ego autem sperábo in te, Dómine.
verses.eng: 54:24 Bloody and deceitful men shall not live out half their days; * but I will trust in thee, O Lord.

ant_sexta.label: Antíphona
ant_sexta.lat: In Deo sperávi * non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
ant_sexta.eng: In God I have put my trust * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.

verses.lat: 55:2 Miserére mei, Deus, quóniam conculcávit me homo: * tota die impúgnans tribulávit me.
verses.eng: 55:2 Have mercy on me, O God, for man hath trodden me under foot; * all the day long he hath afflicted me fighting against me.

verses.lat: 55:3 Conculcavérunt me inimíci mei tota die: * quóniam multi bellántes advérsum me.
verses.eng: 55:3 My enemies have trodden on me all the day long; * for they are many that make war against me.

verses.lat: 55:4 Ab altitúdine diéi timébo: * ego vero in te sperábo.
verses.eng: 55:4 From the height of the day I shall fear: * but I will trust in thee.

verses.lat: 55:5 In Deo laudábo sermónes meos, in Deo sperávi: * non timébo quid fáciat mihi caro.
verses.eng: 55:5 In God I will praise my words, in God I have put my trust: * I will not fear what flesh can do against me.

verses.lat: 55:6 Tota die verba mea exsecrabántur: * advérsum me omnes cogitatiónes eórum in malum.
verses.eng: 55:6 All the day long they detested my words: * all their thoughts were against me unto evil.

verses.lat: 55:7 Inhabitábunt et abscóndent: * ipsi calcáneum meum observábunt.
verses.eng: 55:7 They will dwell and hide themselves: * they will watch my heel.

verses.lat: 55:8 Sicut sustinuérunt ánimam meam, pro níhilo salvos fácies illos: * in ira pópulos confrínges.
verses.eng: 55:8 As they have waited for my soul, for nothing shalt thou save them: * in thy anger thou shalt break the people in pieces.

verses.lat: 55:9 Deus, vitam meam annuntiávi tibi: * posuísti lácrimas meas in conspéctu tuo.
verses.eng: 55:9 O God, I have declared to thee my life: * thou hast set my tears in thy sight,

verses.lat: 55:9 Sicut et in promissióne tua: * tunc converténtur inimíci mei retrórsum:
verses.eng: 55:9 As also in thy promise. * Then shall my enemies be turned back.

verses.lat: 55:10 In quacúmque die invocávero te: * ecce, cognóvi, quóniam Deus meus es.
verses.eng: 55:10 In what day soever I shall call upon thee, * behold I know thou art my God.

verses.lat: 55:11 In Deo laudábo verbum, in Dómino laudábo sermónem: * in Deo sperávi, non timébo quid fáciat mihi homo.
verses.eng: 55:11 In God will I praise the word, in the Lord will I praise his speech. * In God have I hoped, I will not fear what man can do to me.

verses.lat: 55:12 In me sunt, Deus, vota tua, * quæ reddam, laudatiónes tibi.
verses.eng: 55:12 In me, O God, are vows to thee, * which I will pay, praises to thee:

verses.lat: 55:13 Quóniam eripuísti ánimam meam de morte, et pedes meos de lapsu: * ut pláceam coram Deo in lúmine vivéntium.
verses.eng: 55:13 Because thou hast delivered my soul from death, my feet from falling: * that I may please in the sight of God, in the light of the living.

verses.lat: 56:2 Miserére mei, Deus, miserére mei: * quóniam in te confídit ánima mea.
verses.eng: 56:2 Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me: * for my soul trusteth in thee.

verses.lat: 56:2 Et in umbra alárum tuárum sperábo, * donec tránseat iníquitas.
verses.eng: 56:2 And in the shadow of thy wings will I hope, * until iniquity pass away.

verses.lat: 56:3 Clamábo ad Deum altíssimum: * Deum qui benefécit mihi.
verses.eng: 56:3 I will cry to God the most High; * to God who hath done good to me.

verses.lat: 56:4 Misit de cælo, et liberávit me: * dedit in oppróbrium conculcántes me.
verses.eng: 56:4 He hath sent from heaven and delivered me: * he hath made them a reproach that trod upon me.

verses.lat: 56:4 Misit Deus misericórdiam suam, et veritátem suam, * et erípuit ánimam meam de médio catulórum leónum: dormívi conturbátus.
verses.eng: 56:4 God hath sent his mercy and his truth, * and he hath delivered my soul from the midst of the young lions. I slept troubled.

verses.lat: 56:5 Fílii hóminum dentes eórum arma et sagíttæ: * et lingua eórum gládius acútus.
verses.eng: 56:5 The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons and arrows, * and their tongue a sharp sword.

verses.lat: 56:6 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, * et in omnem terram glória tua.
verses.eng: 56:6 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, * and thy glory above all the earth.

verses.lat: 56:7 Láqueum paravérunt pédibus meis: * et incurvavérunt ánimam meam.
verses.eng: 56:7 They prepared a snare for my feet; * and they bowed down my soul.

verses.lat: 56:7 Fodérunt ante fáciem meam fóveam: * et incidérunt in eam.
verses.eng: 56:7 They dug a pit before my face, * and they are fallen into it.

verses.lat: 56:8 Parátum cor meum, Deus, parátum cor meum: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam.
verses.eng: 56:8 My heart is ready, O God, my heart is ready: * I will sing, and rehearse a psalm.

verses.lat: 56:9 Exsúrge, glória mea, exsúrge, psaltérium et cíthara: * exsúrgam dilúculo.
verses.eng: 56:9 Arise, O my glory, arise psaltery and harp: * I will arise early.

verses.lat: 56:10 Confitébor tibi in pópulis, Dómine: * et psalmum dicam tibi in géntibus:
verses.eng: 56:10 I will give praise to thee, O Lord, among the people: * I will sing a psalm to thee among the nations.

verses.lat: 56:11 Quóniam magnificáta est usque ad cælos misericórdia tua, * et usque ad nubes véritas tua.
verses.eng: 56:11 For thy mercy is magnified even to the heavens: * and thy truth unto the clouds.

verses.lat: 56:12 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus: * et super omnem terram glória tua.
